title: Book Two · Chapter 113: The Dry Pages
story:
On Monday, Jun's tree book is dry. It lies open on the reading table. The bottom corner is thick and pale.

Miss Wu puts a clean sheet beside it.

“The words are clear,” she says. “The pages can turn now. Do not force the cover flat.”

Jun turns one page. Then another. A small part of a green leaf has lost its colour. The name beneath it is still there.

The younger boy stands on the other side of the table.

“I can read it to you,” he tells Jun.

“You can read it for yourself,” Jun says. “I can still see the words.”

The boy gives a small uncertain smile.

Ronan takes two coins from his pocket. He puts them beside the book.

“For the damage,” he says.

Jun looks at the coins.

“I do not want your coins.”

“But my wrong time—”

“Your wrong time made us wait. His wet bag made the book wet. I lent him my book. Those are different things.”

Ronan takes his hand away.

“I know they are different. I still want to help.”

“You can correct the guide.”

Miss Wu moves the coins back toward Ronan. She asks the younger boy to return on Tuesday. He and another pupil will practise putting dry covers around books. He agrees. Then he goes to his lesson.

Jun puts the tree book into a plain protective cover. He does it slowly around the thick corner.

The new paper will not lie flat at first. Jun opens the fold a little and tries again.

Ronan starts to put one hand beside the book. Then he leaves it on his own knee.

“Do you need the other paper?”

Jun looks at the clean sheet Miss Wu left.

“Yes. Nearer, please.”

Ronan moves it within reach. Jun takes it and keeps the book in front of himself.

The younger boy is gone now. The coins are beside Ronan's hand again. He closes his fingers around them and puts them in his pocket.

He cannot hear them against the table anymore. Jun is still working with the cover.

One pale part of the leaf shows near the edge of the page. Ronan remembers its brighter colour. A new paper cover will keep the book together, but it will not put that colour back.

He watches Jun make the last small fold. He wants to do something more useful than sit beside him with two coins.

“Can we still do our next page?” Ronan asks.

Jun keeps his eyes on the fold.

“Not together.”

“Only for now?”

“I do not know how long.”

Ronan sits down. The chair makes a loud scrape. He wants to say Jun is being unfair. He wants to say one guide should not end all their work.

Instead he asks, “Can you tell me before you choose someone else?”

Jun looks up at last.

“I can choose my own partner.”

“Yes.”

Jun takes his book and leaves. He carries it under his arm. The damaged corner is against his body.

At home, Ronan returns the two coins to his tin. Mum is nearby with a bag for a customer. She sees his face.

“Did he take them?”

“No.”

“Then that part is his choice.”

Ronan shuts the tin. “I thought it would help.”

“It may help with something else. Ask before you decide.”

Mum turns back to the bag. A long thread catches on her sleeve. Ronan lifts the thread off her sleeve. She thanks him.

He sits beside her. The tin stays closed on the shelf. Mum pulls another thread through the cloth, and he listens to the quiet sound.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

damage＝损坏；protective cover＝保护封套；lend＝借给；partner＝搭档。

## 理解问题

1. Jun怎样区分书受潮和时间谎言？
2. Jun对继续搭档给了什么答复？

## 读句子

**Jun / takes his book / and leaves.** Jun／拿起他的书／离开。
